clue.text: Hardest areas for development — would include this?

definitions.text: Hardest areas for development — would include this?

indicators.note: letters put up for development are rebuilt into a new shape, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A planner's question about which tough regions are ripe for development, suggesting a vast desert would be among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'for development' rearranges HARDEST AREAS, and the world's largest hot desert would certainly include some of the hardest areas to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast North African desert is a textbook case of terrain where building anything is extremely difficult.

clue.text: Shock about reduction in range getting agreement

indicators.note: the shocking word goes about, i.e. around, the other piece

parts.note: to shock someone is to appal them

indicators.note: a reduction cuts the word short, here dropping its final letter

parts.note: to range is to rove or wander widely

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by cuts to a product range nonetheless ends up agreeing to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a line of products, but it is the verb meaning to wander; 'reduction in' drops its last letter, and 'about' wraps the shock word around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is the giving of consent, the same as agreement to a proposal.

clue.text: Some numerals obscured in addition

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the figures are illegible as well, like a smudged ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning 'as well' or 'besides', so one can replace the other in a sentence.

clue.text: A rude lust involving love may make you this

definitions.text: A rude lust involving love may make you this

indicators.note: the rearranged letters involve, i.e. take inside, the extra piece
the letters of the phrase may make something else once reordered, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A moralising warning that crude desire combined with love could lead a person into infidelity.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'may make' rearranges A RUDE LUST to ADULTERUS, and 'involving' slips O inside, while lust mixed with love for another can make one unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driven by lust for a lover outside marriage becomes unfaithful to their spouse.

clue.text: Last fixture must do this

definitions.meaning: to last is to go on or persist
something fixed in place must stay put and hold out over time

explanation.surface: A sports fixture that has to be played out to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue over time, and anything that is a fixture by nature must persist and hold firm.

clue.text: Second in team's very good — in my view the perfect example

indicators.note: Second in picks out the letter in second place of the word that follows

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
'to me' expresses an opinion, as in 'to me it looks fine'

explanation.surface: A fan gushing that the team's second player is so good he is the ideal of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is the person or thing that embodies a quality completely, the model instance of it.

clue.text: Where spirits are in opposition?

definitions.meaning: the afterlife, the realm of the dead that spirits inhabit
being on the opposing team or party in a contest

explanation.surface: A séance quip wondering whether ghosts are against us.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the realm beyond death where ghosts dwell and the opposing camp in any dispute.

clue.text: Firm informed about evidence of special offer

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm
to be 'up on' a subject is to be well informed about it

explanation.surface: A company briefed on proof of a promotional deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher clipped from a paper or flyer is the token that proves you qualify for a discount.

clue.text: TV programme concession involves one

indicators.note: the concession word involves, i.e. wraps around, the next piece

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's concession that includes a single extra show.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial drama on television, so called after the soap-maker sponsors of early radio serials.

clue.text: Confined area, according to Spooner's brief comment

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: bound means tied up or confined
a site is an area of ground

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about a restricted zone, as reported in Spooner's words.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, quotable extract from a speech, used by the media, is a brief comment.

clue.text: It's affected the toes a lot with a trace of fungus

definitions.text: It's affected the toes a lot with a trace of fungus

indicators.note: letters that are affected are disturbed and put into a different order
a trace of a word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A description of a foot infection that has spread among the toes, with a hint of fungal growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges THE TOES A LOT plus F (the first letter, 'a trace of' fungus), and the whole clue also describes the condition itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This common skin complaint is a fungal infection between the toes, exactly what the clue depicts.

clue.text: Suggest tent that's excellent

parts.note: to tip is to suggest, as in tipping a horse to win
a circus tent is the big top

explanation.surface: A camper recommending a tent as first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal adjective for first-rate or of the highest quality.

clue.text: Continue to rant, beginning to traduce Irish parliament

parts.note: to storm on is to keep raging or ranting

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A politician who keeps raging, starting to slander the assembly in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: STORMONT is the Belfast estate housing Northern Ireland's devolved assembly, and its name is used for that parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Northern Ireland Assembly sits in Belfast's parliament buildings, and the building's name stands for the legislature.

clue.text: Most of cold meal served up — Prince tucking in — safe for kids?

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: chill means cold

indicators.note: the prince is tucked inside the turned-around word, as at a table
in a down clue, served up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: food is a meal

explanation.surface: A cold dinner brought out with a royal tucking in, safe enough for children.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'served up' reads the meal word from the bottom, giving DOOF; 'tucking in' seats the prince just after its first letter, and 'Most of' drops the cold word's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A child-proof cap or lock is designed so young children cannot open or damage it, making it safe for them.

clue.text: County, one ready to invest in old money

indicators.note: putting money into something is investing in it, so the funds go inside the currency word

parts.note: lire were Italy's currency before the euro
an means one, as in 'an apple'
ready, as in 'the readies', is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A county with someone prepared to pour funds into old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASHIRE is a county in north-west England; 'ready' for cash is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is one of the historic shire counties of England, around Preston and Lancaster.

clue.text: Quantity of water filling some receptacle

indicators.note: the answer fills, or sits inside, the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some water poured into a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, a body of standing water, chiefly in English place names.

clue.text: Lawyer — a Democrat — about to block election

indicators.note: the 'about' piece blocks the vote by sitting in its middle

parts.note: a vote is an election
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A Democrat lawyer preparing to obstruct an election.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and elsewhere an advocate is a barrister, a lawyer who pleads cases in court.

clue.text: What's closed before ship's launch?

indicators.note: the closed piece comes before the ship

parts.note: a door that is pushed to is closed
SS, steamship, is the standard ship abbreviation

explanation.surface: A question about what gets sealed before a ship is launched.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something is to throw it, and launching a ball or stone is the same act.

clue.text: Slip, early in the day? Almost fell

parts.note: to skid is to slip

indicators.note: almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: dawn is the earliest part of the day

explanation.surface: Someone slipped in the early morning and very nearly fell over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is a noun: in northern England a fell is a hill or mountain, and SKIDDAW is a peak in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiddaw is a mountain in the English Lake District, where such peaks are called fells.

clue.text: Flower rules field after replanting

indicators.note: the letters are replanted in a new order, as a gardener might move plants

explanation.surface: A flower dominating a field once it has been replanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleur-de-lis is the iris or lily, stylised in French heraldry, so it names a flower.

clue.text: Sexual urge beginning to lapse: I offer love

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone whose desire is fading still offers love.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the psychological term for sex drive, the instinctive sexual desire.

clue.text: Designer omitting second note for carpenter?

indicators.note: the second of the two identical letters is left out

parts.note: a planner is one who designs schemes
N is a note, from north on a compass

explanation.surface: A designer who drops one note, wondering about the carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a planer, one who planes wood, is only loosely a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker smoothing boards with a plane is one who planes, a fair cryptic description of a joiner.

clue.text: Clumsily kiss and run in winter sports venue

indicators.note: done clumsily, the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: An awkward kiss and a dash away at the ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste on a snowy mountainside is where skiers descend, the core winter sports venue.

clue.text: Doctor holding eyeball — one's obsessed with death

indicators.note: the doctor holds the other pieces between his two letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor
orb is a poetic word for the eye or eyeball
I is the Roman numeral one, with 's a linking 'is'

explanation.surface: A doctor clutching an eyeball, a person with a ghoulish fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid describes an unhealthy interest in gruesome things such as dying and disease.

clue.text: Greek character taking in new Italian feature

indicators.note: the Greek letter takes in, or contains, the next piece

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person absorbing a fresh Italian trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna, the volcano on Sicily, is a famous landmark of Italian geography.

clue.text: Unconscious after excess drug taken? An anomalous response

indicators.note: the unconscious piece comes after the rest

parts.note: OD is an overdose, an excess of a drug
to be done is to be taken in or cheated
someone out cold is unconscious

explanation.surface: Someone knocked out after an overdose, and an unusual reaction to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The item that does not fit with the rest of a group is the anomaly, such as one answer unlike all others.

clue.text: One director enthralled by 'Carmen', maybe, or other opera

indicators.note: the pieces are held captive inside the other one

parts.note: car men are motorists, members of the AA, the British Automobile Association
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A director captivated by Bizet's Carmen, or perhaps by some other opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' wants to be Bizet's opera, but split it as car men: motorists, whose British motoring club is the AA (Automobile Association).
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Egyptian tragedy is an opera other than Carmen, the work the surface names.

clue.text: Cracked elbow, for a bet? Folly of Biblical proportions

indicators.note: cracked means broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who broke their elbow on a wager, an act of epic foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Genesis story tells of a hubristic tower meant to reach heaven, an overreaching folly in the Bible.
